text: Tata Motors overtook Mahindra & Mahindra to become India's second‑largest passenger‑vehicle maker by domestic dispatches in the April‑Sept 2026 period, with its dispatches surging 43% to over 3.9 lakh units versus Mahindra's just under 3.6 lakh units (around 20% growth). Mahindra's BE and XEV models jumped 82% to 42,338 units, lifting their share of passenger‑vehicle volumes from 7.8% to 11.8%, while Tata benefited from a 59% surge in utility‑vehicle dispatches. The overall passenger‑vehicle market grew 28.3% to around 26.4 lakh units.

Stellantis India, Tata Motors Passenger Vehicles Limited (TMPV) and its subsidiary Tata Passenger Electric Mobility Limited (TPEM) signed a Definitive Agreement on Monday to expand their partnership into advanced vehicle technology and architecture, with TMPV providing access to its product technology and vehicle architecture for Stellantis to develop for more than 50 global markets. The vehicles will be manufactured in India at Fiat India Automobiles Private Limited (FIAPL), the 50:50 joint venture between TMPV and Stellantis in Pune, according to a company statement. Shailesh Chandra, Managing Director & CEO of TMPV, said the agreement marks an important next step, while Tianshu Xin, COO of Stellantis Asia‑Pacific, said it will help develop competitive vehicles in India and expand export potential across international markets. (Published on October 12, 2026)

text: Tata Motors overtook Mahindra & Mahindra to become India’s second‑largest passenger‑vehicle manufacturer in April‑Sept FY27, dispatching over 3.9 lakh units (+43% YoY) versus Mahindra’s just under 3.6 lakh units (+20%). The gain was driven by a 59% surge in utility‑vehicle dispatches. Overall domestic passenger‑vehicle dispatches rose 28.3% YoY to around 26.4 lakh units.
If completed, the acquisition would create a global commercial‑vehicle group with roughly €21 billion in annual revenue and about 5,90,000 vehicles sold per year.

Tata Motors expanded its partnership with Stellantis, signing a definitive agreement on 12 October 2026 to give Stellantis access to Tata’s product technology and vehicle architecture. The collaboration will develop vehicles in India for more than 50 global markets, with manufacturing at Fiat India Automobiles Private Limited, the 50:50 joint venture between the two companies in Pune.
